# I2C FSM Behavioral Design Specification

## 1. Overview

The I2C FSM module is the protocol engine for an I2C controller that can operate as an I2C host or as an I2C target. It controls the serial clock line and the serial data line, generates and detects START, repeated START, and STOP conditions, transmits and receives bytes, handles ACK/NACK signaling, and provides status and event outputs to the rest of the system.

The module is intended to operate in one mode at a time: either host mode or target mode. Host mode and target mode shall not both be active simultaneously.

The module shall support 7-bit target addressing, standard I2C signaling, clock stretching by targets, and automatic clock stretching by the target when required.

---

## 2. Reset and Idle Behavior

After reset, the module shall:

- release both bus lines to the high (released) state;
- remain idle until an operating mode is enabled and a triggering condition occurs;
- assert that both the host and target are idle;
- not assert any event or FIFO request outputs.

The module leaves the idle state when:

- host mode is enabled and a format FIFO entry is available; or
- target mode is enabled and a START condition is detected on the bus.

The host idle indication shall be asserted whenever no host transaction is in progress. The target idle indication shall be asserted whenever no target transaction is in progress.

---

## 3. Bus Line Driving Behavior

The module shall drive the clock and data lines according to I2C protocol behavior. A high output corresponds to a released line, and a low output corresponds to an actively driven line. The module shall only pull lines low and shall release them high when no device should drive them.

All bus timing shall be derived from the programmed timing configuration, including:

- high and low periods of the clock line;
- rise and fall time allowances;
- START setup and hold times;
- data setup and hold times;
- STOP setup time;
- bus-free time before a new START.

The module shall respect these timing constraints while generating START, STOP, data, and ACK signaling.

---

## 4. Host Mode Behavior

### 4.1 Format FIFO Entries

While in host mode, the module consumes entries from the format FIFO. Each format entry contains:

- a byte to transmit or a read count;
- a START-before flag;
- a STOP-after flag;
- a read flag;
- a read-continue flag;
- a no-ACK-OK flag.

The module shall process each entry as follows:

- If no flags are set, transmit the byte and wait for an ACK from the target.
- If the START flag is set, issue a START or repeated START condition before handling the byte.
- If the STOP flag is set, issue a STOP condition after the byte or read operation is complete.
- If the read flag is set, treat the byte as an unsigned count and read that many bytes from the target.
- If the read-continue flag is set, ACK the final byte of the read; otherwise NACK the final byte.
- If the no-ACK-OK flag is set, do not report a missing ACK as an error.

A read count of zero shall be interpreted as 256 bytes.

### 4.2 START and STOP Generation

The module shall generate a START condition by pulling the data line low while the clock line is high, after the programmed setup time.

The module shall generate a repeated START when a START flag is processed and the previous transaction was not terminated by a STOP. A repeated START shall be treated as the end of the previous transaction, and the transaction-complete event shall be asserted at that point.

The module shall generate a STOP condition by holding the data line low while the clock line is low, releasing the clock line, and then releasing the data line after the programmed setup and bus-free time. The transaction-complete event shall be asserted when the STOP condition is complete.

After a STOP, the module shall wait for the required bus-free time before starting another transaction.

### 4.3 Byte Transmission

When transmitting a byte, the module shall:

- drive the data line with each bit, MSB first;
- ensure data is stable while the clock line is high;
- generate the appropriate clock high and low phases for each bit;
- after the eighth bit, release the data line and generate the ACK clock pulse;
- sample the data line during the ACK pulse to determine whether the target acknowledged.

If the target does not drive the data line low during the ACK pulse:

- the NAK event shall be asserted, unless the no-ACK-OK flag is set;
- the module shall continue to the next format entry regardless of the NAK condition.

### 4.4 Read Operations

When processing a read entry, the module shall:

- read the specified number of bytes from the target;
- place each received byte into the receive FIFO and assert a receive FIFO write when the byte is complete;
- ACK all bytes except the final byte;
- NACK the final byte unless the read-continue flag is set.

If the read-continue flag is set, the final byte shall also be ACKed so the target continues sending. After the final byte, the module shall either issue a STOP or advance to the next format entry, depending on the STOP flag.

### 4.5 Format FIFO Flow

The module shall request the next format FIFO entry when the current entry has completed and the bus is at a byte boundary.

If host mode is disabled at a format boundary, the module shall terminate the bus activity with a STOP and return to the idle state.

### 4.6 Host Mode Events

In host mode, the module shall assert the following events when the corresponding condition is detected:

- **NAK event**: a transmitted byte did not receive an ACK, and the no-ACK-OK flag was not set.
- **Transaction complete**: a STOP condition has completed, or a repeated START has been issued.
- **SCL interference**: the clock line is observed to fall while the host is driving it high during a clock pulse. Normal clock stretching, where the clock line is held low before the host releases it, shall not be treated as interference.
- **SDA instability**: the data line changes while the clock line is high during data or ACK sampling.
- **SDA interference**: the host is enabled and idle but the data line is low, or the host is driving the data line high and the line remains low after the programmed rise time has elapsed.
- **Stretch timeout**: a target holds the clock line low longer than the programmed timeout, and timeout detection is enabled.

---

## 5. Target Mode Behavior

### 5.1 START/STOP Detection and Address Matching

While in target mode, the module shall detect START, repeated START, and STOP conditions based on data line transitions while the clock line is high.

After detecting a START, the module shall receive the first byte, which contains the 7-bit target address and the read/write bit. The address shall be compared against two configurable address/mask pairs.

For an address to match:

- each bit where the mask bit is 1 shall equal the corresponding configured address bit;
- each bit where the mask bit is 0 shall match the configured address bit only if the configured address bit is also 0;
- if a mask bit is 0 and the configured address bit is 1, that address pair shall be incapable of matching any received address.

If the received address does not match either configured address pair, the module shall not acknowledge and shall return to the idle state.

If the address matches, the module shall:

- place an acquire FIFO entry containing the received address byte and a START indication;
- if the read/write bit indicates a read and the transmit FIFO is empty, assert the TX-empty event;
- acknowledge the address in accordance with the clock-stretching rules below.

### 5.2 Write and Acquire Operations

When the target accepts a write transaction (read/write bit = 0), the module shall:

- acknowledge the address;
- receive each subsequent data byte;
- place each received data byte into the acquire FIFO;
- acknowledge each received data byte;
- continue until a STOP or repeated START condition is received.

If the acquire FIFO is full, the target shall stretch the clock by holding the clock line low until space becomes available.

When a STOP or repeated START is detected, the module shall place an acquire FIFO entry that indicates the transaction-ending condition and then return to the idle state.

### 5.3 Read and Transmit Operations

When the target accepts a read transaction (read/write bit = 1), the module shall:

- acknowledge the address;
- take the next byte from the transmit FIFO and drive it onto the data line, MSB first;
- after transmitting eight bits, release the data line during the ACK bit and sample the host ACK/NACK.

If the host acknowledges:

- the module shall fetch the next transmit byte and continue transmitting.

If the host NACKs:

- the module shall wait for a STOP or repeated START condition;
- when the STOP or repeated START arrives, the module shall place an acquire FIFO entry indicating the condition and the host NACK/ACK status;
- if the transmit FIFO still contains data at the end of the transaction, the module shall assert the TX-nonempty event;
- if the host sends a STOP or repeated START immediately after an ACK rather than after a NACK, the module shall assert the ACK-stop event.

If the transmit FIFO is empty when a byte is needed, the target shall stretch the clock by holding the clock line low and assert the TX-empty event until data is written to the transmit FIFO.

### 5.4 Target Clock Stretching Controls

The target shall automatically stretch the clock in two cases:

- when a read transaction requires data and the transmit FIFO is empty;
- when a write transaction receives data and the acquire FIFO is full.

The target may also support optional address-stretch behavior. If enabled for transmit transactions or acquire transactions, the target shall stretch the clock after matching its address and before acknowledging that address.

If the corresponding stop-stretch control is asserted, the target shall not stretch for that address match and shall acknowledge immediately. After using the stop-stretch control for one matched address, the module shall indicate that the stop-stretch control should be cleared so that subsequent address matches stretch again.

### 5.5 Target Mode Events

In target mode, the module shall assert the following events when the corresponding condition is detected:

- **TX-empty**: a read transaction needs data and the transmit FIFO is empty.
- **TX-nonempty**: a read transaction ends while data is still present in the transmit FIFO.
- **ACK-stop**: the host sends a STOP or repeated START after an ACK instead of after a NACK.
- **Host timeout**: during an active target transaction, the clock line remains high for longer than the configured host timeout, measured from the last low-to-high transition of the clock line.

---

## 6. Event Summary

The module shall provide event indications for the following conditions:

| Event | Assertion Condition |
|---|---|
| NAK | Host transmitted a byte and received no ACK, and no-ACK-OK was not set |
| Transaction complete | STOP complete or repeated START issued |
| SCL interference | Clock line falls while host is driving it high during a clock pulse |
| SDA interference | Host enabled and idle with data line low, or data line fails to rise while host drives it high |
| SDA unstable | Data line changes while clock line is high during sampling |
| Stretch timeout | Target holds clock low beyond the programmed timeout with timeout enabled |
| TX empty | Target read needs data and transmit FIFO is empty |
| TX nonempty | Target read ends with data remaining in transmit FIFO |
| ACK-stop | Host ends a target read with STOP/repeated START after ACK |
| Host timeout | Host leaves clock high too long during an active target transaction |

---

## 7. Conclusion

The I2C FSM module shall implement the required host and target protocol behavior, including START/STOP generation, byte and bit transfers, ACK/NACK handling, FIFO interaction, clock stretching, timeout detection, and event reporting. All behavior shall conform to the I2C protocol requirements and to the timing configuration supplied by software.
